To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nitrous oxide is an inhibitor of vitamin B12 in vivo and in vitro and that the inhibition of vitamin B12 is the basis for the inhibition of growth in the absence of methionine or when methionine synthase is inhibited by sulfanilamides.

nitrous oxide inhibitory activity of the methionine synthase reaction, and the inhibition of microbial growth by nitric oxide, are due to the inactivation of the enzyme by the nitrosylcobalamin intermediate formed in the course of the reaction.

nitrous oxide inhibitory effects on methionine synthase in intact bacteria are not due to a nitrosation reaction and that the inactivation of methionine synthetase by nitrous oxide is irreversible and is not prevented by the presence of methionine in the growth medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vitamin B12 (cobalamin, Cbl) in microbial growth and metabolism.
the development and evaluation of new methods for the detection of nitrous oxide in the presence of oxygen.
the mechanism of action of nitrous oxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth-inhibition effect is not a direct effect on the methionine synthase enzyme but a secondary consequence of the inhibition of methionine synthetase by nitrous oxide.
nitrous oxide is the only gaseous molecule known which can be metabolized by intact cells, and that this metabolism is mediated by a single enzyme.
nitrous oxide inactivates methionine synthase in bacteria by oxidizing cobalt to the +3 oxidation state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N2O is the first known inactivator of the cobalamin-dependent enzyme, methionine synthase.
the inhibition of methionine synthesis by nitrous oxide is due to inactivation of methionine synthase by a nitrous oxide-dependent reaction involving cobalamin.
nitrous oxide is an inhibitor of the methionine synthase reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nitrous oxide is an effective inhibitor of methionine synthase in vivo.
nitrous oxide inhibiting methionine synthesis in E. coli is an important mechanism by which nitrous oxide can inhibit growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.
nitrous oxide is a potent inhibitor of vitamin B12 dependent microbial growth.
